auth.bootstrapHelp: This installation has no accounts yet. The account you create here is an administrator and can manage everything.
auth.passwordRules: At least 12 characters, using at least two of: lowercase, uppercase, digits, symbols.
auth.socketWarning: Access to Iskele is equivalent to root on this host.
auth.totpHint: The six-digit code from your authenticator app.

containers.confirmRemove: Type the container name to confirm removal
containers.confirmRemoveHelp: This removes {{name}} permanently. Anonymous volumes are removed with it.
containers.emptyHelp: Containers you create will appear here.
containers.emptyStopped: No containers are running. Turn on “show stopped” to see the rest.
containers.redeployHelp: Pulls the image again and recreates the container with the same configuration. Anonymous volumes are not preserved.
containers.redeploy_rolled_back: The new container failed; the old one was restored
containers.title: Containers

stats.onlyRunning: Stats are only available for a running container.

console.onlyRunning: A console can only be opened on a running container.

settings.allowed_paths_empty: Empty — every bind mount will be refused.
settings.allowed_paths_hint: The only directories bind mounts and build contexts may use. Read-only here on purpose: widening this from a browser would be one step from mounting the whole filesystem into a container.
settings.audit_retention_forever: Zero keeps every entry. The trail only grows.
settings.audit_retention_hint: Entries older than {{window}} are removed on the next daily sweep.
settings.bind_warning_hint: Shows a warning in the creation wizard whenever a host directory is mounted. A nudge, not a control — the path whitelist is what decides.
settings.installation_defaults: No config file: these are the built-in defaults.
settings.installation_hint: These come from {{file}} and take effect at startup. Change them there and restart.
settings.title: Settings
settings.two_factor_manual: Or type this secret in by hand
settings.two_factor_off: Off. Anyone with your password can sign in as you.
settings.two_factor_on: Enabled. Signing in asks for a code from your authenticator app.
settings.two_factor_qr_alt: QR code for the two-factor secret
settings.two_factor_scan: Scan this with an authenticator app, then enter the code it shows.

errors.forbidden: Your role does not allow this

create.title: Create a container
create.subtitle: Every option `docker run` takes, with a live preview of the command it becomes.
create.image_hint: Repository and tag, e.g. nginx:1.27 or ghcr.io/org/app:v2.
create.name: Container name
create.name_hint: Leave empty to let the engine pick one.
create.start_now: Start the container after creating it
create.auto_remove: Remove the container when it exits
create.init: Run an init process as PID 1
create.command_hint: Overrides the image CMD. Quotes are honored.
create.ports_empty: No published ports. The container will only be reachable from other containers.
create.host_ip_hint: Leave empty to publish on every interface, which reaches the network this host is on.
create.mounts_empty: No volumes. Anything written inside the container is lost when it is removed.
create.allowed_paths_none: No allowed_paths are configured, so bind mounts are refused entirely.
create.path_outside: {{path}} is outside the allowed paths and will be refused.
create.paste_env_hint: One KEY=value per line. Comments and export prefixes are handled.
create.aliases_hint: Extra DNS names for this container, comma-separated.
create.ipv4_hint: Only works on a network with a user-defined subnet.
create.cpus_hint: 1.5 means one and a half cores.
create.cpu_shares_hint: Relative weight under contention. The default is 1024.
create.health_disable: Disable the health check the image defines
create.health_test_hint: Run through a shell, e.g. curl -f localhost/health.
create.log_driver_hint: Leave empty for the daemon default.
create.privileged_title: These options can give the container the host
create.privileged_allowed: You hold the privileged permission. Each option below removes part of what keeps a container inside its own namespace.
create.privileged_denied: These need the privileged permission, which your role does not have. The server will refuse a container that uses them.
create.privileged_hint: Disables nearly all isolation. Equivalent to root on the host.
create.cap_drop_hint: Narrows the container, so it needs no special permission.

images.empty_hint: Pull one above, or create a container and let the engine fetch it.
images.tag_hint: A second reference to the same image. The original tag stays.
images.remove_hint: Any stopped container built from it will no longer start.
images.prune_hint: Only images with no tag of their own. Tagged images are kept.
images.run: Create a container from this image

volumes.empty_hint: A volume keeps data alive when the container using it is removed.
volumes.remove_hint: The data in it goes with it. There is no undo.
volumes.prune_hint: An unused volume may still be the only copy of a database. Nothing here can tell the difference.

networks.internal_hint: Internal: no route to the outside world
networks.connect_hint: The container joins this network in addition to the ones it is already on.
networks.remove_hint: The engine refuses while containers are still attached.
networks.prune_hint: Only user-defined networks with nothing attached. bridge, host and none are kept.

registries.title: Private registries
registries.subtitle: Credentials for pulling images the public registries do not serve.
registries.empty_hint: Public images need none of this. Add one when a pull is refused with "unauthorized".
registries.password_hint: Encrypted with the master key before it is stored, and never sent back.
registries.password_keep: Leave empty to keep the stored password.
registries.remove_hint: Pulls from it will fall back to anonymous access.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.empty: Nothing running. Finished tasks are kept for ten minutes.

users.delete_message: Deletes {{username}} and ends every session it holds. This cannot be undone.
users.none_hint: Every account here can sign in to this panel.
users.password_hint: At least 12 characters, with at least two of: lowercase, uppercase, digit, symbol.
users.reset_totp_message: Clears two-factor for {{username}} and ends their sessions. Use this when the device that produces their codes is gone.
users.role_admin_hint: Everything, including accounts, settings and privileged container options.
users.role_operator_hint: Create, start, stop and remove containers; no accounts, no privileged options.
users.role_viewer_hint: Read-only. Can look at everything and change nothing.
users.title: Users

audit.none_yet: Actions taken through this panel will appear here.
audit.title: Audit log

prune.containers_rule: Removes every container that is not running or paused. Their logs go with them; their volumes do not.
prune.description: Each of these deletes things nobody named individually, so each one asks first.
prune.images_rule: Removes untagged image layers no container references. Tagged images are kept, so nothing has to be pulled again.
prune.networks_rule: Removes user-defined networks with no containers attached. The engine defaults are kept.
prune.title: Reclaim disk space
prune.volumes_rule: Removes every volume no container is using. A volume holds data that is not coming back from anywhere — check that nothing stopped is meant to start again.

build.browse_truncated: This directory has more entries than can be listed; the rest are not shown.
build.dockerfile_hint: Relative to the context directory. Empty means Dockerfile.
build.forbidden_hint: Building runs whatever the Dockerfile says, as root, inside the daemon. It takes the build permission, which your role does not have.
build.history_empty_hint: A build started here stays in the history for 180 days; its output is kept for 30.
build.no_cache_hint: Rebuild every layer, even ones that have not changed.
build.platform_hint: Build for another architecture, if the engine can.
build.problem_dockerfile: The Dockerfile must be inside the context directory.
build.problem_tag: An image reference cannot contain spaces.
build.pull_hint: Fetch a newer FROM image even when one is already present.
build.run_image: Create a container from this image
build.section_args_hint: Values for the Dockerfile's ARG instructions. They are visible in the image's history — do not put secrets here.
build.section_context_hint: The directory sent to the engine, minus whatever .dockerignore excludes.
build.section_image_hint: What the build produces, and how it is produced.
build.section_labels_hint: Metadata written onto the built image.
build.subtitle: Build a Dockerfile from a directory on this host. Only the whitelisted paths can be used as a context.
build.tags_hint: One or more image references, separated by commas. A build with no tag produces an untagged image.
build.target_hint: The multi-stage stage to stop at.
build.title: Build an image

stacks.discovered: Running here, not managed by Iskele
stacks.discovered_hint: Compose projects started with the docker CLI on this host. Importing adopts the record; the containers keep running untouched.
stacks.down_hint: Stops and removes this stack's containers. The stack itself stays, so it can be deployed again.
stacks.down_volumes_hint: A volume is the one part of a stack that cannot be recreated. A database's data lives there.
stacks.editor_subtitle: Compose files are parsed with the same library the docker CLI uses, then deployed over the engine socket — no docker compose binary needed.
stacks.empty_hint: A stack is a compose file Iskele deploys for you. Write one here, read one from this host, or clone a repository.
stacks.engine_error: Docker is not reachable, so what is actually running cannot be shown. The compose file below is still the stack's.
stacks.env_hint: Values for ${...} in the compose file. This is the only place they resolve from — never the daemon's own environment.
stacks.forget_hint: Removes the record and its working copy. Containers are left alone — take the stack down first if you want them gone.
stacks.git_url_hint: https, ssh, or git@host:org/repo. Private repositories must not need a password prompt.
stacks.name_fixed: The name labels every container this stack creates, so it cannot change.
stacks.no_services: This stack has no services yet.
stacks.parse_error: This stack's compose file no longer parses
stacks.path_hint: Must be inside allowed_paths. An .env beside it is read too.
stacks.path_in_repo_hint: Relative to the repository root. Empty finds compose.yaml on its own.
stacks.source_hint: Where the compose file comes from. A file or repository is copied in on save, so what deployed stays knowable after the working tree moves on.
stacks.validate_hint: Check the file to see what would happen. It runs the same checks a deploy runs, including the path whitelist.

catalog.network_hint: Attach to an existing network so other containers can reach this one by name.
catalog.no_matches_hint: Try a different category, or search for what the application does rather than its name.
catalog.privileged_blocked_hint: It sets capabilities, devices, sysctls or host networking, which take the privileged permission. Declaring them in a template does not grant them.
catalog.start_hint: Off creates the container and leaves it stopped.
